title: Part Four, Chapter 6: The Journey to the East

verses.t: And then they set about going there to the East, seeking to fulfil what their fathers had commanded them, which they had not forgotten. And their fathers had been dead a long time when they married and took fathers-in-law and took wives, the three of them. And they said as they went, "Let us go to the East, where our fathers came from!" And the three sons took the road: one was called Gocaib, son of Balam-quitzé, of all the people of Caviquib; the other Goacutec, son of Balam-acab, of the people of Nihaibab; and the other was called Gohaan, son of Mahucutah, of the people of Ahan-Quiché. And these were the names of those who went over there to the other side of the sea. Three were those who went, and they knew what they were doing, and they were not men of no account. And they took leave of all their brothers and kinsmen and went off very joyfully, and said, "We shall not die, but we shall come back," the three said as they went. And so they crossed over the sea and came there to the East, and they went to receive their kingdom. And this was the name of the lord who ruled in the East, where they went.

And they came before the lord who was called Nacxit, a great lord, one who judged all things, and great was his kingdom. And he gave them the sign of his kingdom, of all the diviners. And then came the sign of the great lords and of the lords of the houses, and then came the sign of the greatness of the great lords; and Nacxit finished giving them everything, the diviners and the form of the kingdom. And this was all of it: the throne, the flute, the cham-cham (another flute), jades, tzicvil, cohtzicvil, balam-bolom, head, pich-quech, macutax, toltatam, quz, buz, caxcom, chiyon, aztapulul. And they brought it all on their backs when they came; and they brought from the other side of the sea their writing and paintings of Tulanzú. They left their writing to these, for much is what they set down in their traditions.

And then, when they came to their town, which was called Hacavitz, all those of Tanub and Ylocab and all the peoples gathered there, and rejoiced at the coming of Gocaib, Goacutec and Gohaan. And there they took up again the lordship of the peoples; and those of Rabinal, the Cakchiquels and those of Quiquinaha rejoiced; and they displayed the signs and symbols of their kingdom that they had brought. And great was their power over the peoples, and it had no end, when they displayed the signs of their empire. And they were there at Hacavitz, and with them all those who had come from the East, who had gone on that long journey; and on the mountain they were now very many. And there the wives of Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah died. And when they came, they left that dwelling of theirs and looked for another place to settle; and the mountains they lived on, as they multiplied and increased and wandered, could not be counted. And our first fathers and mothers gathered together, said the ancients, when they told of the first town they abandoned, which was called Hacavitz. And then they came to settle another, which was called Chiquix, or the thorns, and they stayed a long time on that other town, and there they multiplied and had sons and daughters. And there they were on many hills, which were four, and they gave their town the name of only one. And they married off their sons and daughters; they only gave them away, and took the price of their daughters only as a token of thanks; and the life they had was good. And then each of the tribes passed on from those hills: Fac, or "many," was the name of Quix, the one; another was Chichat, another Humetaha, another Culba and another Rabinal; these were the names of the hills where they stopped. They were looking for the hills of the town they sought, and they were now very many. And those who had gone to receive the empire in the East had already died; they came from there already old to each of the towns, and they were not found on those mountains when the others passed. And they suffered many hardships, because they found their town very far away; they were grandfathers and fathers. And this is the name of the town where they came.
